name: launch-simple
about: The default launch film, 15-30 s: lines and pictures that meet, never a slideshow. The first line alone on a lit ground, then the product doing what it said; the next lines arrive with their pictures (the picture standing far behind the line, centred and soft, coming up into focus as it leaves), and pictures between play alone (a pair with no line: at most four lines a film); the claim alone on its colour field, the hero line; then a centred lockup built from the last picture with the one fact under it. Every change of picture carries something (a camera move across the cut, the picture falling back under the next line, one object flying from one scene into the next): the frame is never empty between two scenes. Two or three dealt creative elements (src/fx/creative) take at least half the beats with the product inside them, so it is never a line, then a card; the camera moves only with a purpose and rests under them. One text voice, one ground family, three or four seam kinds, everything fitted to the music's bars and the script's lines. The agent writes the script (src/launch.ts), fetches the input shot (tools/input.mjs) and writes the product's scenes (src/product.tsx); the timeline, the seams, the ground, the end card and the sound plan follow. new-film.sh lays these files over the Remotion starter (the default for --format launch).

beats.T: a line alone, centred in the middle band, on a clean ground (launch.ts beat 'alone'; it builds over the last picture as that one falls back): 0.5-2.4 s (about 1.3), one entry voice for the film
beats.A: the product or the picture acting, full frame, centred, no statement over it: 1-3.5 s, varied (a long one beside a short one); a pair with no line is one A beat, carried on from the last picture
beats.TA: a line with its picture: the picture far behind it, centred, smaller, soft and dim, then coming up and racking into focus as the line leaves (beat 'with'), or the line held over a picture composed round it (beat 'over'): at most 40 % of the beats
beats.end: the centred lockup built from the last picture's element, the one fact under it, held 2-3 s
beats.mix: unset, the first line and the claim alone, the lines between with; aim for about T 25 % / T+A 30 % / A 37 % (timeline.ts BEAT_MIX): one 'over' in a film of four or five lines gets there

deal.seed: the deck's direction when scripts/deck.py dealt one in this project (it writes src/dealt.ts: one source), else the product's name (IDENTITY.name) or launch.ts seed; launch.ts pin fixes a slot by hand
deal.print: npx tsx -e "import { DEAL, DEAL_SOURCE } from './src/deal'; console.log(DEAL_SOURCE); import { SEAM_PLAN, BEAT_PLAN, BEAT_MIX } from './src/timeline'; console.log(DEAL, SEAM_PLAN.map((s) => s.recipe), BEAT_PLAN.map((b) => b.kind + ' ' + ((b.to - b.from) / 60).toFixed(2)), BEAT_MIX)"

slots.creative: two or three of src/fx/creative (deal.ts CREATIVE: scripts/deck.py writes them into src/dealt.ts, else the name deals them), never a recent film's set; timeline.ts CREATIVE_PLAN puts them on at least half the beats

music.about: Every launch is cut to a licensed, human-made, instrumental track (references/music.md): the track carries the film and its cuts, earshot effects mark the picture's own moments (each line whole, the product's clicks and results, the seams that move, one hit on the lockup); never effects only. Any tempo from 90 to 140 BPM fits: the timeline fits each line and picture to the track's beats and each pair to whole bars.
music.pick: node scripts/music.mjs pick --mood "<the film's mood words>" --length <s> (a launch here: 115-136 BPM and the film's energy preferred; the curated library; with none, music.mjs search --bpm 115-136), then music.mjs get '#n' --to audio/music (its licence record beside it; never the last film's track)
music.add: bash scripts/new-film.sh <dir> --music <file> --title T --artist A --source S --page URL --licence L --seen-quote Q --seen-url URL --ai-generated no --vocals no, or later: python3 scripts/audio/track.py add <file> ...
then: python3 scripts/audio/track.py fit   (after launch.ts is written: the film's bars, the lockup's bar and the cuts read from the timeline at the track's tempo; the edit plays exactly those bars, lands the entry on the lockup, keeps sections from changing mid-shot, ends on a hit; then src/music.ts)
npm run music fits again after a change to the script or the track

next: simple launch: write the script in src/launch.ts (3-5 pairs: a line of 2-7 words and the picture that proves it; line 1 says what the product does by name; how each line meets its picture, `beat` alone, with or over (unset: the first and the last alone, the others with); the strings each picture shows; the one fact for the end card; `input`, the core action in plain words) and the product's name in src/brand/identity.ts,
fetch the input shot: node tools/input.mjs (the footage recipe for launch.ts input, else a search in its words; it writes src/input.ts; --pick <n> after a look, --none "<why>" when no footage fits),

build each picture in src/product.tsx from the product's real screens (the first one shows its core change literally: input -> output), each with its focus box, one object carried from scene to scene (SceneDef carry, IDEA), the last one with its hero element,

see the deal: run deck.py here once (its direction and the film's creative elements become src/dealt.ts, the one deal the film plays; with none, the name deals), then npx tsx -e "import { DEAL, DEAL_SOURCE, CREATIVE } from './src/deal'; import { CREATIVE_PLAN } from './src/timeline'; console.log(DEAL_SOURCE, DEAL, CREATIVE, CREATIVE_PLAN)" (launch.ts pin fixes a slot); give each creative element what it needs on its pair (alts, logos, before, count) and each scene its focus box,
then the music (below), npm run check, and a contact sheet of out/preview.mp4 against references/checks.md (the placement, beat and seam gates)
